claim: Myomaker (Tmem8c) is a muscle-specific membrane protein necessary for fusion of embryonic and adult muscle progenitors.
source: Myomaker (Tmem8c) is a muscle-specific membrane protein necessary for fusion of embryonic and adult MPs (Millay et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Millay et al., 2013

claim: In adult muscle, myomaker expression is undetectable at baseline but rapidly induced in satellite cell descendants after cardiotoxin injury.
source: In adult muscle, myomaker expression is undetectable but rapidly induced in SC descendants after cardiotoxin (CTX) injury.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge from prior work

claim: Myomaker mRNA and protein are acutely induced after muscle overload in wild-type mice.
source: In wild-type (WT) mice at baseline, myomaker mRNA and protein are not readily detected in muscle, however myomaker is acutely induced after MOV (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: Supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 1A and B

claim: Myomaker expression peaks 7 days after muscle overload.
source: Expression of myomaker peaked 7 days after MOV, and was down-regulated at later time points.
evidence: Based on temporal analysis of myomaker expression shown in Figure 1A and B

claim: Myomaker is expressed in muscle progenitors during the early stages of muscle overload (days 3 and 7).
source: Quantification of these populations multiple days after MOV revealed an increase in myomaker-expressing MPs at the early stages of MOV (days 3 and 7), followed by a reduction at later stages of MOV (days 10 and 14) (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by X-gal staining and quantification in Tmem8cLacZ/+ mice shown in Figure 1C

claim: The majority of LacZ+ myofibers are observed at later stages of muscle overload (days 7-14).
source: In contrast, the majority of LacZ+ myofibers were observed at later stages of MOV, with negligible occurrence at 3 days after MOV.
evidence: Based on quantification of LacZ+ myofibers in Figure 1C

claim: Labeling of fusion-competent muscle progenitors during the first 7 days of muscle overload results in a greater percentage of myofibers containing a BrdU+ nucleus compared to labeling during the final 7 days.
source: Labeling of fusion-competent MPs during the first 7 days of MOV resulted in a greater percentage of myofibers containing a BrdU+ nucleus compared to labeling during the final 7 days of MOV (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by BrdU incorporation assay shown in Figure 1D

claim: Myomaker expression was efficiently deleted in myomaker scKO muscle 7 days after muscle overload.
source: qPCR analysis confirmed the efficiency of this tamoxifen-based strategy, as myomaker expression was eliminated in myomaker scKO muscle compared to control muscle 7 days after MOV (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2A

claim: The myomaker scKO model does not significantly alter the frequency of muscle stem cells during muscle overload.
source: These results indicate that while there could be subtle alterations in SC dynamics, the myomaker scKO model does not significantly alter the frequency of muscle stem cells.
evidence: Based on flow cytometry and Pax7 immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2

claim: Ablation of myomaker in satellite cells results in restriction of myomaker expression to muscle progenitors and lack of expression in the myofiber.
source: X-gal staining of plantaris sections from myomaker scKO mice after MOV demonstrates that myomaker expression is restricted to non-myofibers (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by X-gal staining data shown in Figure 2B

claim: There is an accumulation of LacZ+ non-myofibers at 7 days post-MOV in myomaker scKO mice compared to control mice.
source: Quantification of LacZ+ non-myofibers revealed an accumulation at 7 days post-MOV in myomaker scKO mice compared to control mice, reflecting the inability of myomaker-deficient MPs to fuse to myofibers (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by quantification of LacZ+ cells shown in Figure 2B

claim: LacZ in myofibers in control mice is contributed through fusion of muscle progenitors.
source: We also observed a lack of LacZ activity in myofibers in myomaker scKO mice at days 7–14 of MOV, suggesting that LacZ in myofibers in control mice is contributed through fusion of MPs (Figure 2B).
evidence: Inferred from the absence of LacZ in myofibers when MPs cannot fuse, shown in Figure 2B

claim: Myomaker is not actively transcribed from a myofiber nucleus in response to muscle overload.
source: Overall, these data indicate that myomaker is not actively transcribed from a myofiber nucleus in response to MOV.
evidence: Based on genetic deletion experiments using myofiber-specific Cre shown in Figure 2C

claim: Myomaker mKO MOV plantaris did not exhibit a reduction in myomaker levels compared to control MOV.
source: However, myomaker mKO MOV plantaris did not exhibit a reduction in myomaker levels compared to control MOV, whereas a reduction was achieved in myomaker scKO MOV plantaris (Figure 2C).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2C

claim: Plantaris weight normalized to tibia length reveals a two-fold increase in control MOV compared to sham.
source: Following 14 days of overload, evaluation of plantaris weight normalized to tibia length revealed a two-fold increase in control MOV compared to sham (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by muscle weight measurements shown in Figure 3B

claim: Myomaker scKO MOV plantaris was smaller than control MOV.
source: In contrast, myomaker scKO MOV plantaris was smaller than control MOV, although still increased above myomaker scKO sham weight (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by muscle weight measurements shown in Figure 3B

claim: Control mice show an increase in myofiber size after muscle overload.
source: Indeed, through histological examination of the plantaris after MOV, in control mice we observed an increase in myofiber size, a more direct evaluation of hypertrophy (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by histological analysis and CSA measurements shown in Figure 3C

claim: Myofiber hypertrophy is not observed in myomaker scKO MOV plantaris sections.
source: This characteristic was not observed in myomaker scKO MOV plantaris sections, highlighting the importance of myomaker on MPs for efficient hypertrophy (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by histological analysis and CSA measurements shown in Figure 3C

claim: No differences in myofiber cross-sectional area were detected between myomaker scKO sham and MOV.
source: In contrast, no differences were detected between myomaker scKO sham and MOV, indicating defective myofiber hypertrophy following MOV with genetic deletion of myomaker in MPs (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by CSA quantification shown in Figure 3C

claim: Genetic ablation of myomaker in satellite cells results in a lack of hypertrophy of Type IIa, IIb, and IIx myofibers.
source: This analysis revealed no differences in fiber type frequency after MOV, and that genetic ablation of myomaker in SCs resulted in a lack of hypertrophy of Type IIa, IIb, and IIx myofibers (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by fiber type-specific CSA analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: The total number of fibers is elevated in control MOV compared to control sham mice.
source: Furthermore, the total number of fibers is elevated in control MOV compared to control sham mice, but fiber number is similar between sham and overloaded muscles in myomaker scKO mice (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by fiber number quantification shown in Figure 3D

claim: Fiber number is similar between sham and overloaded muscles in myomaker scKO mice.
source: Furthermore, the total number of fibers is elevated in control MOV compared to control sham mice, but fiber number is similar between sham and overloaded muscles in myomaker scKO mice (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by fiber number quantification shown in Figure 3D

claim: Myomaker-deficient muscle progenitors are unable to fuse to each other to generate de novo myofibers.
source: These data suggest an inability of myomaker-deficient MPs to fuse to each other to generate de novo myofibers, indicating a distinct requirement for myomaker in augmenting fiber number during the response to overload.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of increase in fiber number in myomaker scKO mice shown in Figure 3D

claim: Satellite cell-derived myomaker is required for load-induced adult skeletal muscle hypertrophy.
source: Collectively, our findings demonstrate the requirement of satellite cell-derived myomaker for load-induced adult skeletal muscle hypertrophy.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple experimental results showing impaired hypertrophy in myomaker scKO mice

claim: After 14 days of overload in control mice, BrdU+ nuclei within a dystrophin-stained myofiber were readily detected.
source: After 14 days of overload in control mice, BrdU+ nuclei within a dystrophin-stained myofiber were readily detected (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by BrdU immunostaining shown in Figure 4B

claim: In overloaded myomaker scKO mice, BrdU+ nuclei reside primarily in the interstitium between myofibers.
source: In comparison, BrdU+ nuclei reside primarily in the interstitium between myofibers in overloaded myomaker scKO mice, indicating efficient abrogation of fusion (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by BrdU immunostaining shown in Figure 4B

claim: Approximately 30% of myofibers in control mice underwent a fusion event during muscle overload.
source: Indeed, quantification of the percentage of BrdU+ myofibers revealed ~30% of myofibers in control mice underwent a fusion event, however in myomaker scKO mice BrdU+ myofibers are at basal levels observed in shams (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by quantification of BrdU+ myofibers shown in Figure 4B

claim: The majority of existing myofibers in control mice undergo fusion with muscle progenitors after muscle overload.
source: After muscle overload the majority of existing myofibers in control mice undergo fusion with MPs, evaluated by expression of both mTom and mGFP, which was not observed in overloaded myofibers of myomaker scKO mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by genetic lineage tracing using Rosa26mTmG reporter shown in Figure 4D

claim: There is a significant increase in mGFP intensity of single fibers in control mice after overload, which is reduced to sham levels after genetic ablation of myomaker in muscle progenitors.
source: Here, we detected a significant increase in mGFP intensity of single fibers in control mice after overload, which is reduced to sham levels after genetic ablation of myomaker in MPs (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by quantification of mGFP intensity in isolated single fibers shown in Figure 4E

claim: Expansive muscle progenitor fusion occurs during load-induced skeletal muscle hypertrophy.
source: Our overall findings substantiate that expansive MP fusion occurs during load-induced skeletal muscle hypertrophy, and that myomaker expression on MPs is essential for this myogenic process.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from BrdU and genetic lineage tracing experiments shown in Figure 4

claim: Myomaker-mediated fusion is necessary for myofiber hypertrophy in response to physiological stimuli.
source: Moreover, these results indicate that myomaker-mediated fusion is necessary for myofiber hypertrophy in response to physiological stimuli.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments showing lack of hypertrophy in fusion-defective muscle

claim: Control MOV muscles show an increase in phosphorylated levels of Akt (Ser473) and p70s6k (Thr389) at 7 and 14 days of overload.
source: To this end, western blot analysis revealed an expected increase in phosphorylated levels of Akt (Ser473) and p70s6k (Thr389) in control MOV muscles at 7 and 14 days of overload (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5A

claim: Activation of Akt and p70s6k pathways is significantly blunted in myomaker scKO overload muscle.
source: Activation of these pathways was significantly blunted in myomaker scKO overload muscle, highlighting a mechanism by which myomaker expression on MPs regulates hypertrophy (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by western blot data and quantification shown in Figure 5A

claim: Total levels of p70s6k are elevated in control MOV muscles compared to myomaker scKO overload muscles.
source: Additionally, total levels of p70s6k were elevated in control MOV muscles compared to myomaker scKO overload muscles, which could be indicative of enhanced overall protein translation in control MOV samples during hypertrophy (Bakker et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5A and citation to Bakker et al., 2016

claim: Puromycin is elevated in both myh3- (existing) and myh3+ (de novo) myofibers 7 days after MOV in control muscle.
source: We observed minimal puromycin in sham samples, however in control muscle puromycin was elevated in both myh3- (existing) and myh3+ (de novo) myofibers 7 days after MOV (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by puromycin immunostaining shown in Figure 5B

claim: At 14 days of MOV, puromycin remains elevated in existing fibers of control mice, whereas myomaker scKO muscle does not exhibit significant puromycin incorporation.
source: At 14 days of MOV, we detected minimal myh3+ myofibers although puromycin remained elevated in existing fibers of control mice, whereas myomaker scKO muscle did not exhibit significant puromycin incorporation at either time point analyzed (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by puromycin immunostaining and quantification shown in Figure 5B

claim: Myh3+ cells are not observed in myomaker scKO muscle 7 days after MOV.
source: Of note, we did not observe myh3+ cells in myomaker scKO muscle 7 days after MOV, further demonstrating that myomaker is required to form new myofibers (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by myh3 immunostaining shown in Figure 5B

claim: Fusion-incompetent muscle has a significant inability to activate protein synthesis.
source: Given that myh3+ myofibers are not present in myomaker scKO muscle we only quantified the puromycin intensity in myh3- myofibers, which revealed a significant inability for fusion-incompetent muscle to activate protein synthesis (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by quantification of puromycin intensity shown in Figure 5B

claim: Satellite cell-derived myomaker is required for full activation of Akt/mTOR signaling and protein synthesis in the myofiber.
source: Our findings indicate that SC-derived myomaker is required for full activation of Akt/mTOR signaling and protein synthesis in the myofiber, which could serve as a potential mechanism though which fusion drives the hypertrophic response.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from western blot and puromycin incorporation data shown in Figure 5

claim: Control MOV muscle shows modest fibrosis, indicating that ECM remodeling is a normal process for hypertrophy.
source: We performed Masson's Trichrome staining on control and myomaker scKO sham and MOV muscle, which revealed modest fibrosis in control MOV, indicating that ECM remodeling is a normal process for hypertrophy (Figure 6).
evidence: Supported by Masson's Trichrome staining shown in Figure 6

claim: There is an increase in fibrosis in the overloaded muscles of myomaker scKO mice.
source: In contrast, we observed an increase in fibrosis in the overloaded muscles of myomaker scKO mice (Figure 6).
evidence: Supported by Masson's Trichrome staining and quantification shown in Figure 6

claim: The enhanced accumulation of ECM in myomaker scKO MOV muscle may explain the increase in muscle weight despite the lack of myofiber hypertrophy.
source: Consequently, the enhanced accumulation of ECM in myomaker scKO MOV muscle may explain the increase in muscle weight despite the lack of myofiber hypertrophy (Figure 3).
evidence: Inferred from fibrosis data in Figure 6 and muscle weight data in Figure 3

claim: Fusion has a protective role in stabilizing muscle architecture associated with increased workload.
source: This non-functional gain in muscle size illustrates that in place of de novo and larger myofibers, there is an increased formation of connective tissue in muscles with non-fused MPs, suggesting a protective role for fusion in stabilizing muscle architecture associated with increased workload.
evidence: Inferred from the increased fibrosis observed in fusion-defective muscle shown in Figure 6

claim: Fusion of skeletal muscle stem/progenitor cells is required for proper development and regeneration.
source: Fusion of skeletal muscle stem/progenitor cells is required for proper development and regeneration, however the significance of this process during adult muscle hypertrophy has not been explored.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge

claim: Genetic deletion of myomaker in muscle stem cells results in a complete reduction of overload-induced hypertrophy.
source: We rendered muscle progenitors fusion-incompetent through genetic deletion of myomaker in muscle stem cells and observed a complete reduction of overload-induced hypertrophy.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from the study

claim: The blunted hypertrophic response in myomaker scKO mice is associated with a reduction in Akt and p70s6k signaling and protein synthesis.
source: This blunted hypertrophic response was associated with a reduction in Akt and p70s6k signaling and protein synthesis, suggesting a link between myonuclear accretion and activation of pro-hypertrophic pathways.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from the study shown in Figure 5

claim: Fusion-incompetent muscle exhibits increased fibrosis after muscle overload.
source: Furthermore, fusion-incompetent muscle exhibited increased fibrosis after muscle overload, indicating a protective role for normal stem cell activity in reducing myofiber strain associated with hypertrophy.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from the study shown in Figure 6

claim: Satellite cells reside underneath the basal lamina in a quiescent state.
source: SCs reside underneath the basal lamina in a quiescent state, and upon injury, become activated to generate a pool of myogenic progenitors (MPs) that differentiate and fuse to each other or existing myofibers to restore structure and function to muscle (Relaix and Zammit, 2012; Yin et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Relaix and Zammit, 2012 and Yin et al., 2013

claim: Satellite cells are clearly necessary for efficient regeneration after acute injury.
source: While SCs are clearly necessary for efficient regeneration after acute injury (Günther et al., 2013; Lepper et al., 2011; Sambasivan et al., 2011), the role of SCs during adult muscle hypertrophy and maintenance is much less understood.
evidence: Supported by citations to Günther et al., 2013; Lepper et al., 2011; Sambasivan et al., 2011

claim: Skeletal muscle hypertrophy occurs when the rates of muscle protein synthesis exceed those of protein degradation.
source: Fundamentally, skeletal muscle hypertrophy occurs when the rates of muscle protein synthesis exceed those of protein degradation.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge

claim: Myonuclear accretion precedes an increase in skeletal muscle size.
source: Moreover, myonuclear accretion precedes an increase in skeletal muscle size (Bruusgaard et al., 2010), and loss of serum response factor (Srf) in the myofiber blunts hypertrophy potentially through a SC-mediated mechanism (Guerci et al., 2012), altogether implicating a role for fusion during hypertrophy.
evidence: Supported by citations to Bruusgaard et al., 2010 and Guerci et al., 2012

claim: Studies utilizing diphtheria toxin-mediated ablation of satellite cells have revealed that effective myofiber hypertrophy occurs in the absence of satellite cells.
source: Studies utilizing diphtheria toxin (DTA)-mediated ablation of SCs have revealed that effective myofiber hypertrophy occurs in the absence of satellite cells and that SCs are not required to maintain muscle mass during aging (Fry et al., 2015; McCarthy et al., 2011), however SC ablation leads to impaired coordination and diminished muscle performance (Jackson et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Fry et al., 2015; McCarthy et al., 2011; Jackson et al., 2015

claim: A recent report indicates that effective myofiber hypertrophy does not occur in the absence of satellite cells.
source: Recently, a report utilizing a similar DTA SC ablation model indicates that effective myofiber hypertrophy does not occur in the absence of SCs (Egner et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Egner et al., 2016

claim: There is no consensus regarding the contributions of satellite cells during adult skeletal muscle hypertrophy.
source: Thus, there is no consensus regarding the contributions of SCs during adult skeletal muscle hypertrophy, highlighting the need for more independent models that assess the biology of SC activity.
evidence: Stated as a summary of conflicting literature

claim: Fusion is more efficient if both fusing cells express myomaker.
source: Here, all MPs exhibit upregulation of myomaker, and we have shown that fusion is more efficient if both fusing cells express myomaker (Millay et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Millay et al., 2016

claim: The Akt1 pathway activates mTOR and p70s6k and ultimately leads to enhanced protein synthesis.
source: An established mechanism for eliciting muscle hypertrophy is through the Akt1 pathway, which activates mTOR and p70s6k and ultimately leads to enhanced protein synthesis (Egerman and Glass, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Egerman and Glass, 2014

claim: The BrdU analysis may underestimate the extent of fusion that occurs during muscle overload.
source: Given that this is one level of a muscle, if a BrdU myonucleus was above or below this plane then that fiber would not be counted as a positive fusion event. Therefore, this BrdU analysis may underestimate the extent of fusion that occurs during MOV.
evidence: Logical inference about the limitations of the BrdU method

claim: The BrdU strategy is an underestimation of the fusion process during muscle hypertrophy compared to the fluorescent reporter model.
source: While BrdU analysis revealed approximately 30% of fibers to undergo a fusion event, findings from the fluorescent reporter model demonstrate that the majority of myofibers fuse (mGFP+), indicating the BrdU strategy is an underestimation of the fusion process during muscle hypertrophy.
evidence: Comparison of results from two different experimental approaches (BrdU vs. genetic reporter)

claim: Myofibers have the ability to intrinsically activate the Akt/mTOR protein synthesis pathway.
source: The inability for muscle to initiate Akt/mTOR signaling without myomaker expression in myogenic progenitors was surprising since previous studies have shown that myofibers have the ability to intrinsically activate this canonical protein synthesis pathway (Bodine et al., 2001; Lai et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bodine et al., 2001 and Lai et al., 2004

claim: Satellite cell activation is not observed during muscle hypertrophy induced through a constitutively active Akt transgene.
source: Indeed, SC activation is not observed during muscle hypertrophy induced through a constitutively active Akt transgene (Blaauw et al., 2009), or inhibition of myostatin action by pharmacological blockade of its receptor ACVR2B (Lee et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Blaauw et al., 2009 and Lee et al., 2012

claim: During overload-induced hypertrophy, the increased tension placed on the myofiber requires satellite cell-mediated activity for hypertrophy.
source: It is conceivable that during overload-induced hypertrophy, the increased tension placed on the myofiber requires SC-mediated activity for hypertrophy, whereas there is an absence of mechanical strain on the myofiber through treatment with IGF-1 or ACVR2B antibody.
evidence: Speculative reasoning about the mechanism

claim: Hypertrophy associated with loss of myostatin may not yield long-term improvements in muscle function.
source: Hypertrophy associated with loss of myostatin may not yield long-term improvements in muscle function suggesting that addition of myonuclei are necessary for functional hypertrophic gains (Gundersen, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gundersen, 2016

claim: DTA-mediated deletion of satellite cells results in increased ECM components during overload-induced hypertrophy and aging.
source: DTA-mediated deletion of SCs also results in increased ECM components during overload-induced hypertrophy and aging, potentially through lack of interactions between SCs and fibroblasts (Fry et al., 2014; Judson et al., 2013; Murphy et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Fry et al., 2014; Judson et al., 2013; Murphy et al., 2011

claim: The main function of muscle progenitors during overload-induced hypertrophy is to release miR-206-containing exosomes that dampen collagen production in fibroblasts.
source: Indeed, recent work suggests that the main function of MPs during overload-induced hypertrophy is to release miR-206-containing exosomes that dampen collagen production in fibroblasts, and that loss of MPs facilitates development of fibrosis (Fry et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Fry et al., 2017

claim: Muscle progenitors are still present in muscle after overload of myomaker scKO mice.
source: After overload of myomaker scKO mice, MPs are still present in muscle, suggesting the major reason for fibrosis can be attributed to an inability to maintain myofiber integrity due to loss of SC activity.
evidence: Based on flow cytometry and immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2

claim: Fibrosis occurs in myomaker scKO MOV muscles due to an inability to repair myofiber mechanical strain.
source: However, given that no evidence exists supporting this possibility, and that we observed significant fusion during MOV, our data are more consistent with a model where fibrosis occurs in myomaker scKO MOV muscles due to an inability to repair myofiber mechanical strain.
evidence: Inference based on experimental data and reasoning

claim: In cardiac muscle subjected to pressure overload, fibrosis functions to maintain tissue architecture.
source: This model of myofiber mechanical strain eliciting fibrosis is not unlike what occurs in other contexts, such as in cardiac muscle subjected to pressure overload where fibrosis functions to maintain tissue architecture (Creemers and Pinto, 2011; Teekakirikul et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Creemers and Pinto, 2011 and Teekakirikul et al., 2012

claim: Myomaker is activated on satellite cells allowing fusion with a myofiber during muscle hypertrophy.
source: In conclusion, we have shown that myomaker is activated on SCs allowing fusion with a myofiber during muscle hypertrophy, thereby promoting hypertrophic signaling pathways and minimizing fibrosis associated with mechanical strain.
evidence: Summary conclusion from the study's findings

claim: Myomaker activation on satellite cells promotes hypertrophic signaling pathways and minimizes fibrosis associated with mechanical strain.
source: In conclusion, we have shown that myomaker is activated on SCs allowing fusion with a myofiber during muscle hypertrophy, thereby promoting hypertrophic signaling pathways and minimizing fibrosis associated with mechanical strain.
evidence: Summary conclusion from the study's findings

claim: The findings may lead to new intervention strategies for muscle wasting diseases.
source: These findings modify current theories for the role of muscle stem cells during hypertrophy and may lead to new intervention strategies for muscle wasting diseases.
evidence: Speculative statement about potential applications

claim: Tmem8cLacZ/+ mice contain a LacZ cassette in intron 1 of the myomaker locus.
source: Briefly, Tmem8cLacZ/+ mice contain a LacZ cassette in intron 1 of the myomaker locus.
evidence: Description of the mouse model used in the study

claim: In the Tmem8cLacZ/+ system, LacZ serves as a readout for myomaker transcription but not myomaker localization.
source: Thus, in this system LacZ serves as a readout for myomaker transcription but not myomaker localization.
evidence: Explanation of how the genetic reporter system works

claim: No statistical differences in body weights were observed after tamoxifen treatment in either control or myomaker scKO mice.
source: No statistical differences in body weights were observed after tamoxifen treatment in either control or myomakerscKO mice.
evidence: Control measurement reported in the methods

claim: The myonuclear domain postulates a coordinated increase between myonuclei number and cytoplasm volume in order to maintain a constant domain size.
source: The contribution of SCs for hypertrophy was initially justified through the concept of the myonuclear domain (Cheek et al., 1965), which postulates a coordinated increase between myonuclei number and cytoplasm volume in order to maintain a constant domain size (Snow, 1990; Tamaki et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cheek et al., 1965; Snow, 1990; Tamaki et al., 1996

claim: IGF-1 directly activates the Akt pathway.
source: IGF-1 directly activates the Akt pathway (Rommel et al., 2001) while myostatin is a negative regulator of muscle mass through SMAD-dependent inhibition of Akt (Sartori et al., 2009; Trendelenburg et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rommel et al., 2001

claim: Myostatin is a negative regulator of muscle mass through SMAD-dependent inhibition of Akt.
source: IGF-1 directly activates the Akt pathway (Rommel et al., 2001) while myostatin is a negative regulator of muscle mass through SMAD-dependent inhibition of Akt (Sartori et al., 2009; Trendelenburg et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Sartori et al., 2009 and Trendelenburg et al., 2009
